For several weeks in each of those years, the deep current turned around and ran the other way — a reversal, most of a month each time. item.prompt: [Academic Talk — Primatology] According to the professor, how did the monkeys' use of the sleeping cliffs change after the road opened?

item.passage: Transcript: A logging road opened along the Vireno ridge five years ago, and we have followed the macaque groups through it. Start with the sleeping cliffs. We expected desertion. Instead, all four cliffs stayed in use — including the one nearest the roadbed — and the groups kept their old rotation among them, no cliff more crowded than before. Not once in five years was a group found bedding in the canopy. What changed was the clock: groups that settled at dusk now come in well after dark. My colleague Deren reads this as predator response — leopards moving along the new corridor. I think he has it backwards. The wariness he treats as the driver is itself a product of the disturbance — jumpy animals look predator-pressed. The model's pedigree is not the issue — it was built on forest species in forest much like this — but the evidence for it is thinner than for either rival account, and it never fit even our first season's data. A caution about the follow records. Two teams shadowed two groups in parallel, so same-day comparisons exist. Both seasons fell in the same fruiting year, and every ear notch stayed legible to the end. The real limit is habituation: the boldest groups tolerated observers within weeks; the shyest never quite did, and are thin in the record accordingly. The forestry department acted on the report: within a month, crews were setting out rows of quick-growing figs along the bare roadcut. The road stays open at all hours, no second survey was ordered, and nobody has proposed reserve status for the ridge.

item.passage: Transcript: Marthe Dole's notebooks, and what the canal company's toll ledgers add. One entry matters most: a payment to M. Dole, for computing the cuttings — she was paid to calculate, not merely to carry a chain, and that is the whole of my point with the ledgers. They record no purchases of instruments, they place her on the western line — the very stretch where the notebooks later surfaced — and the company archive survives virtually complete; the fire of 1774 never reached the ledger room. Dating the pages was harder. The watermarks tell us nothing — that paper stock was in production for fifty years. The ink is uniform from the first page to the last: one sustained campaign of writing, not several. And the notebooks mention no bridge, no lock, no datable structure at all. What settled it was the binding: nineteenth-century work, far younger than the pages, and once it was set aside, the exposed sewing pattern matched an atelier active only in the 1730s. Now, Odile's objection — that Dole's shortcut fails on steep ground. I accept it. The notebooks flag their own hill pages as doubtful, in Dole's hand. The two hill surveys that survive miss badly against modern measurement, contemporaries used the rival tables on steep ground and got it right, and commissions of the period did hire the shortcut for upland work — the failure is real. After her death, the notebooks went to a schoolmaster at Aubrec, who taught from them for thirty years. They were never separated, their whereabouts are documented in every decade since, and Dole left no heirs.

The trenches sat in natural gravel that had never been disturbed; the new engines were metered, and pressure never rose past the old maximum; and the bursts came in August as often as in January — so much for frost. Notice, though, the inquiry's stamina: chartered for six months, it sat for five years, long after the public anger had died away — that persistence is the real lesson. Its yard tests were matched deliberately to buried conditions; not one gauge of its own went into the ground — the panel worked from testimony; and the laborers were examined as suspects. Why the rival company across the river? Rates. A decade of undercutting had poisoned everything, and the city would not fund repairs whose cost would surface in that rate war — that is why the money stalled. No one from the rival sat on the panel, the rival never bid for the works — the city itself absorbed them in the end — and the report went to the printers on schedule. The recommendations? Hamburg and Turin wrote them into practice within five years; at home they were never written into any code of the period, not even for the new districts, and when steel mains arrived the testing rules carried over unchanged.

item.passage: Transcript: Madariaga spent three years inside the Solana wholesale market, and the study still shapes how we think about informal order. His conclusion on the prized corner positions: seniority. Years on the floor decided who moved up when a pitch fell vacant — an order everyone could recite and nobody had written down. Not kinship: sons ranked behind longer-tenured newcomers, and the best pitches did not run in families. Not chance: he hunted for a lottery and found the traders laughing at the idea. Not hidden favors either: the fee books enter every transfer, dated, each matching the seniority queue exactly. Now, the months behind a stall of his own. Readers long puzzled over the silence in his field notes; the explanation is homely — minding the stall left no hand free to write, and the gap is exactly those months. The committee never admitted him; the account before and after keeps its cool distance perfectly; and the pre-dawn auctions he never saw — his stock came by consignment at midday. Bahn's objection, that the traveling vendors are missing, I concede: the census sheets stop at the permanent stalls. And Bahn's list was compiled in the study's final year. But the matters at issue were the fixed positions, where the travelers held no claim, and the omission leaves the central claim standing. The move to the new hall in 1954 is the coda: within a year the surrounding streets held more stalls than the hall did, the city's numbered plan inside was ignored from the first week, the seniority order never re-formed indoors, and not one dispute reached the municipal courts.
